pages.raw_text: Open Source / Overview Open Source Overview Copy page Run Negentro on your own infrastructure with full control over your data, configuration, and deployment environment. Open Source Self-hosted Developer Infrastructure Negentro Open Source gives you the flexibility to run the intelligence infrastructure on your own environment while keeping control over your data and configuration. Developers can install the SDK directly into an application, or run a self-hosted server as an independent service. Both approaches let you configure storage, embeddings, and model providers to match your existing infrastructure. The stack is designed to be extended through APIs and integrations, allowing you to connect existing databases, plug in custom model providers, and build workflows that fit your deployment requirements. Run Negentro your way As a library Install the SDK directly into your application for embedded memory without external dependencies. As a self-hosted server Run Negentro as an independent service with control over infrastructure, storage, models, and configuration. Get started Python Quickstart Install the negentro-memory package and verify that hybrid memory storage and retrieval work in a few lines of code. Learn more → Node.js Quickstart Install the @negentro/sdk package and connect your first stateful agent workflow. Learn more → Self-hosted server Deploy the Negentro Docker container locally or on your Kubernetes cluster and configure your bitemporal infrastructure. Learn more → Web Studio Launch the visual administrative dashboard to inspect live memories, debug scoring, and browse entities. Learn more → Go further Configure components Configure BYOK routing, embedding providers, pgvector storage, and tune the UnifiedScorer. Learn more → Self-hosting features Explore enterprise namespace isolation, semantic cache purging, and redaction tools. Learn more → Build with cookbooks Use practical examples for LangChain agents, CrewAI, MCP server integrations, and compliance. Learn more → ℹ Need a managed alternative? Compare the self-hosted open-source deployment with the fully managed Negentro Cloud Platform, or switch to the Platform documentation . Default components Negentro ships with sane, production-ready defaults for each part of the pipeline. Every component can be replaced or explicitly configured to match your existing VPC infrastructure and provider preferences. Storage PostgreSQL (Bitemporal KG) Tracks valid_at real-world validity alongside system time. Metadata cache Redis Low-latency session caching and rate limit coordination. Providers Multi-Provider BYOK Routing Natively handles OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Ollama. [2] Negentro Server → Dispatches across Memory Engine , Retrieval Engine , Embedder , and LLM Routing . [3] Your Infrastructure → Your private PostgreSQL database with pgvector , Redis cluster, and VPC model endpoints. code_blocks.title: quickstart.py
code_blocks.code:
from negentro import Memory

# 1. Initialize embedded memory
m = Memory()

# 2. Add memories for a specific user
m.add(
    "User prefers dark mode UI and works primarily with React and TypeScript.",
    user_id="usr_9918",
    metadata={"category": "preferences"}
)

# 3. Retrieve relevant context
results = m.search(
    query="What frontend framework does the user like?",
    user_id="usr_9918",
    limit=3
)

for mem in results["results"]:
    print(f"Score: {mem['score']} | Content: {mem['memory']}")

code_blocks.title: agent_integration.py
code_blocks.code:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from negentro.integrations.langchain import NegentroMemory

# Plug Negentro directly into LangChain agents
memory = NegentroMemory(user_id="alex_204")
llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o")

# Memory automatically syncs after each turn
context = memory.load_memory_variables({"prompt": "What did we discuss earlier?"})

sections.heading: Docker Compose Deployment
paragraphs: Spin up a complete Negentro instance with PostgreSQL (pgvector) and Redis in seconds:

version : '3.8' services : negentro-server : image : negentro/server:latest ports : - "8080:8080" environment : - PORT = 8080 - DATABASE_URL = postgresql://negentro:secret@postgres:5432/negentro - REDIS_URL = redis://redis:6379 - OPENAI_API_KEY =${ OPENAI_API_KEY } - ENABLE_STUDIO = true depends_on : - postgres - redis postgres : image : pgvector/pgvector:pg16 environment : - POSTGRES_USER = negentro - POSTGRES_PASSWORD = secret - POSTGRES_DB = negentro volumes : - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data redis : image : redis:7-alpine volumes : - redisdata:/data volumes : pgdata : redisdata : Run the stack with:

sections.heading: Health & Observability
bullets: GET /readyz — Readiness probe validating PostgreSQL and Redis connectivity.
GET /metrics — Prometheus endpoint tracking query latency, cache hit rates, and embedding throughput.

code_blocks.title: docker-compose.yml
code_blocks.code:
version: '3.8'

services:
  negentro-server:
    image: negentro/server:latest
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      - PORT=8080
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://negentro:secret@postgres:5432/negentro
      - REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
      - OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}
      - ENABLE_STUDIO=true
    depends_on:
      - postgres
      - redis

  postgres:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=negentro
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret
      - POSTGRES_DB=negentro
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    volumes:
      - redisdata:/data

volumes:
  pgdata:
  redisdata:

code_blocks.title: Terminal
code_blocks.code:
docker compose up -d
# Negentro API ready at http://localhost:8080
# Web Studio ready at http://localhost:8080/studio

pages.title: Web Studio
pages.lead: A visual administrative interface and debugger for inspecting memories, tuning retrieval parameters, and managing users.

sections.heading: What is Web Studio?
paragraphs: Web Studio is a lightweight, responsive admin dashboard bundled directly into Negentro. It allows engineering teams to visualize what their AI agents are remembering in real-time, test semantic queries, and inspect raw embedding vectors without opening database shells.

sections.heading: Launching Web Studio
paragraphs: If you are running the self-hosted Docker container, navigate directly to http://localhost:8080/studio . Alternatively, run the standalone studio CLI:

code_blocks.title: Terminal
code_blocks.code:
# Run standalone Web Studio pointing to any Negentro instance
npx @negentro/studio --server http://localhost:8080

cards.title: Memory Explorer
cards.description: Filter memories by user ID, agent ID, session, or tags. Inspect bitemporal timestamps ( valid_at vs system_at ) and edit facts directly.

cards.title: Retrieval Playground
cards.description: Test live queries with side-by-side comparisons of Dense Vector vs BM25 keyword search. Adjust the alpha slider and observe Reciprocal Rank Fusion scores.

cards.title: Knowledge Graph Viewer
cards.description: Interactive 2D/3D visualization of entity nodes and relationships extracted from conversation histories.

cards.title: Audit & Privacy Redaction
cards.description: Verify automated PII and PHI redaction rules. Inspect revision histories to understand how conflicting facts were resolved.

sections.heading: Database Migrations
paragraphs: Execute database schema updates directly from the CLI:

# Run database migrations
negentro db upgrade

Relational Tier → PostgreSQL or SQLite storing memory revisions, user identifiers, raw conversational inputs, and audit records. 2. Graph Tier → PiyGraph tracking real-world facts with separate valid_at and system_at timestamps. 3. Cache Tier → Redis storing hot memory buffers, sliding-window rate limit counters, and semantic query caches. pages.raw_text: Open Source / Reranking UnifiedScorer & Reranking Copy page Combine dense semantic similarity, sparse BM25 text match, recency decay, and cross-encoders for precision retrieval. Reranking UnifiedScorer Reciprocal Rank Fusion BM25 The 3-Stage Reranking Pipeline Stage 1: Candidates → Retrieve Top 50 vectors (HNSW) alongside Top 50 BM25 trigram full-text matches. Stage 2: Fusion → Merge candidates using Reciprocal Rank Fusion ( RRF_K=30 ) to prevent keyword or dense bias. Stage 3: Scoring → UnifiedScorer evaluates 11 weighted signals (similarity, text match, recency decay, contradiction penalty, and pinned weight).
